request.spec:
A steward can undo the last rollover on the same sheet-today it was made (a button;
ROLLOVER_UNDONE fy=<old FY>): the periods it generated are removed and the opening balances it set
are taken back. A later day, anyone else, or a generated period that a claim now belongs to is
refused with an error.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can undo the last rollover on the same sheet-today it was made (a button;
ROLLOVER_UNDONE fy=<old FY>): the periods it generated are removed and the opening balances it set
are taken back. A later day, anyone else, or a generated period that a claim now belongs to is
refused with an error.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The rollover undo is in, and `bin/e2e` now passes all 4 tests in the spec (the main "rollover undo" test plus the three scenario tests).

**How it works**
- A new **Undo last rollover** button (`rollover-undo`) sits next to the rollover button. When it works, the periods that rollover generated are deleted, the opening balances it set are taken back, and it writes `ROLLOVER_UNDONE sheet=… by=… fy=FY2026` to the audit file.
- Each rollover is now saved in the database (new migration `V124__rollover.sql`, entity `Rollover`): who made it, the sheet-today it was made on, the year, the periods it generated, and the opening balances it added.
- The undo is refused with `rollover-error`, and nothing is written, when:
  - the user isn't a steward, or isn't the one who made the last rollover;
  - the sheet-today has moved on since it was made;
  - it has already been undone;
  - any claim on the sheet, voided claims included, now falls in one of the generated periods.
- Only the latest rollover can be undone. Once it's undone, a second press is refused rather than reaching back to an earlier rollover.
- "Belongs to a period" uses the claim's due-by date, as the rest of the app does. If the first new-year period existed before the rollover, it isn't deleted; the opening amounts are just subtracted from it.
- Server: `PeriodService.undoRollover` and the endpoint `POST …/periods/rollover/undo`. Front end: `Periods.undoRollover()`, and the period list drops the removed periods.

**Two changes outside the request itself, both needed for the spec to pass:**
1. **Rolling the same year over again no longer adds the opening balance twice.** The test rolls FY2026 over a second time on a later day and expects no new `OPENING_SET` line and no doubled balance. A rollover now adds only the part of each person's opening that an earlier, not-undone rollover of that year hasn't already added. If the amount owed has dropped since, that difference is negative, so it would be written as a negative opening adjustment. No test covers that case.
2. **A viewer pressing "Generate monthly periods" now shows "Made 0" instead of an error.** This failure wasn't caused by my change: the existing app refused the action for viewers, but scenario 1 expects it to go through and create nothing. I copied what plan generation already does ("A viewer's generate makes none"). It still writes nothing, and the fiscal-year and quarters generate buttons still refuse viewers. This does change how viewers are treated, so you may want to look at it.
